reader.requirement: At 85 an END-CALL closes the CALL begun by the most recently preceding unterminated CALL (either format, with or without ON OVERFLOW / [NOT] ON EXCEPTION), so a statement after END-CALL belongs to the enclosing statement and a CALL ... END-CALL is an imperative (delimited scope) statement admissible inside another statement's imperative-statement; a CALL with a conditional phrase and no END-CALL is a conditional statement there and is refused; a stray END-CALL is a syntax error.

edition-consulted.switches: ConstructRegistry.IsAvailable(edition, call-on-overflow-removed-2023): at 85 the CALL ON OVERFLOW format associates under the Proved reading; at 2023 only by the superset last-resort reading, then refused
CallOnOverflowRemoved2023 check (COBOL0882 at 2023, silent at 85); END-CALL itself is not gated

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: only the ON OVERFLOW phrase the delimited CALL may carry (accepted at 85, COBOL0882 at 2023); the END-CALL scope delimiting, nesting and the conditional-statement refusal are the same code at every edition

reader.notes: Both witnesses MATCH at 85. The grammar closes a CALL with END_CALL? after the one conditionalPhrases loop, ConditionalStatements.IsConditional treats a CALL with a phrase and its END-CALL as imperative, and ProcedureFormatPass refuses the undelimited form inside an imperative-statement. Aside, not this rule: COBOL2796's message cites §2023:14.5.1 at --std 85 instead of the 1985 text.
